chunks: It is narrated from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:

I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while a man owed me money, and I had feared its loss. So I complained of that to him, and he said to me: “When you arrive in Makkah, perform a tawaf on behalf of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and pray two rakʿahs for him; and perform a tawaf on behalf of Abū Ṭālib and pray two rakʿahs for him; and perform a tawaf on behalf of ʿAbdullāh and pray two rakʿahs for him; and perform a tawaf on behalf of Āminah, the mother of Muḥammad, and pray two rakʿahs for her; and perform a tawaf on behalf of Fāṭimah bint Asad and pray two rakʿahs for her. Then supplicate to Allah, Mighty and Exalted, that He return your money to you.”
He said: So I did that, then I went out from the gate of al-Ṣafā, and there was my debtor standing, saying: “O Dawud, you detained me; come and take your money.”

key_terms.ادْعُ: make du'a, calling upon Allah in supplication
key_terms.بَابِ الصَّفَا: the gate of al-Ṣafā, mentioned as the place where he found his debtor
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of salat (prayer) offered after tawaf
key_terms.طَوَافًا: circumambulation of the Kaʿbah performed on behalf of another person
key_terms.غَرِيمِي: my debtor, the one owing the money
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or money owed to the narrator

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe seeking the return of lost or withheld money through worship and du'a in Makkah?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imām al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructed Dawud al-Raqqi to perform tawaf and two rakʿahs on behalf of distinguished forebears of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, then make du'a for the recovery of his owed wealth. The report highlights devotional acts in Makkah, honoring the family connected to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and seeking Allah’s aid in restoring financial rights.
